directive: Reissue a coherence-safe, solver-authored repair after the rejected round-1 bundle. Do not reuse the defective M>a+1 restriction or the constant-baseline nonadaptation proof. For `lem:boundary-bump` and `thm:minimax-lower`, use the maximal normalization-compatible condition M>=a+1, since equality admits g_S identically a+1; keep the boundary bump as an explicitly constructed proof object, never an assumed crux. For `thm:nonadaptation`, build both the source-bump and target-density perturbation around one common nonconstant smooth armwise-regression baseline so the target perturbation has genuinely nonzero contrast and yields the claimed m^{-1/2} separation; compute that separation rather than asserting it. Separately reissue the independently truth-directed corrections as a coherent closure: remove the false global Holder-IPM diagnostic from `thm:ricot-attainment`; if the global process proof genuinely requires s>1/2, state that standard primitive smoothness scope transparently and synchronize all consumers; and correct `def:bias-aware-interval`/`thm:fixed-class-honesty` so the finite zero-standard-error case is a well-defined data-evaluable interval, without gerrymandering the class or assuming optimizer stability. Preserve all valid prior content and proofs, and return exact proposal selectors plus complete provisional proofs for fresh adjudication.

changed.reason: The previous zero-standard-error branch returned \(\mathbb R\), so it had infinite length and contradicted the theorem's finite expected-length claim. The product of the standard error and the folded-normal critical value has continuous limit \(\widehat B_{h,J}+\widehat E_{h,J}\) as the standard error decreases to zero, which gives the finite data-evaluable branch.

Consequently its boundary bias, source stochastic term, and target empirical term are respectively \(O(n^{-1/2})\), \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\), and \(O_P(m^{-1/2})\), giving the ordinary two-sample root-risk reduction \(O(m^{-1/2}+n^{-1/2})\).

Under \(t>1/2\) and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), in the special case \(a=0\), \(r(x)=g_T(x)/g_S(x)\) is uniformly bounded, \(h_n=n^{-1/\{2(s+1)\}}\), and
\[
h_n^{s+1}=n^{-1/2},\qquad \int_{h_n}^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx=O(1).
\]
The dual extension in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\) is strictly positive on every held-out \(x\in[h_n,1]\) whenever both training interior measures are nonzero, so the residual correction in \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) does not collapse to zero. Consequently its boundary bias, source stochastic term, and target empirical term are respectively \(O(n^{-1/2})\), \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\), and \(O_P(m^{-1/2})\), giving the ordinary two-sample root-risk reduction \(O(m^{-1/2}+n^{-1/2})\).
changed.reason: The regular-case sanity check must name the corrected separate-sieve estimator. Its risk conclusion remains conditional on the still-open attainment theorem, not on positivity alone.

changed.from: For fixed \((a,s,t,M)\) with \(s>1/2\), \(t>1/2\), and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence satisfying \(m/n\to\kappa\), the interval \(\mathcal I_{h_n,J_n}\), with the finite zero-standard-error convention in the corrected \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\), obeys \[\liminf_{n,m\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h_n,J_n}\}\ge1-\gamma,\] and its maximal expected length is at most \(C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}\). Uniformly over the class, the explicit four-term statistic \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h_n,J_n}^2\) in \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), including the covariance between \(\widehat U^R_{i,h_n,J_n}\) and \(\widehat U^B_{i,h_n,J_n}\), divided by the variance of the corresponding foldwise linear term converges in probability to one. The resulting studentized linear term has Kolmogorov distance \(o(1)\) from \(N(0,1)\), and conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) the law of \(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h_n,J_n}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h_n,J_n}|\) approximates its centered sampling analogue with error \(o(1)\). The threshold \(s>1/2\) gives the finite one-dimensional Hölder entropy integral needed for the displayed global process, the threshold \(t>1/2\) controls the one-dimensional density-ratio calibration sieve, and the product relation controls the separate nuisance-product remainder. These approximations are derived from the product experiment \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\), bounded outcomes, the optimizer leverage bound in \(\mathrm{thm:ricot\text{-}attainment}\), and the entropy of the one-dimensional Hölder ball after spline-calibration projection. The conclusion includes \(a=1\), where the normal approximation is scaled by \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and the \(2M\) boundary-bias envelope remains explicit.
changed.to:
For fixed \((a,s,t,M)\) with \(s>1/2\), \(t>1/2\), and \(s/(2s+1)+t/(2t+1)>1/2\), along every triangular-array sequence satisfying \(m/n\to\kappa\), the interval \(\mathcal I_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), with the finite zero-standard-error convention in \(\mathrm{def:bias\text{-}aware\text{-}interval}\), obeys
\[
\liminf_{n,m\to\infty}\inf_{\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)}\mathbb P_{n,m}\{\tau\in\mathcal I_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\}\ge1-\gamma,
\]
and its maximal expected length is at most \(C\{m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s)\}\). Uniformly over the class, the explicit four-term statistic \(\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}^2\), including the covariance between \(\widehat U^R_{i,h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat U^B_{i,h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), divided by the variance of the corresponding foldwise linear term converges in probability to one. The studentized linear term has Kolmogorov distance \(o(1)\) from \(N(0,1)\), and conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\) the law of
\[
\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h_n,J_{r,n}}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h_n,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}|
\]
approximates its centered sampling analogue with error \(o(1)\). The threshold \(s>1/2\) gives the finite one-dimensional Hölder entropy integral, \(t>1/2\) controls the density-ratio calibration sieve, and the product relation controls the nuisance-product remainder. The conclusion includes \(a=1\), where the normal approximation is scaled by \(\sqrt{\log n/n}\) and the \(2M\) boundary-bias envelope remains explicit.
changed.reason: The inference theorem must name the corrected interval, variance statistic, and multiplier processes after the separate-sieve and untruncated-boundary repair; every empirical approximation remains open.

changed.from: For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set \[\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},\qquad \widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.\] Regress \(Z\) on \(\mathbf b_{h,J}\) using the same training indices with \(X\ge h\), the normalized least-squares objective, and ridge \(n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2\). Define \(\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(x)\) as \(\max\{-1,\min\{1,\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}\}\) for \(x<h\) and as the analogously truncated fitted spline for \(x\ge h\). Define \(\widehat d_{k,h}(x)=\mathbf 1\{|\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}|<1\}\), taking value zero at equality. Empty local samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridge, ordered basis, and stated kink convention make every fold fit and its boundary linearization unique.
changed.to:
For each \(k\in\{1,\ldots,K_0\}\), use the source indices in \(\mathcal T^S_k\) and set
\[
\widehat G_{k,h}=\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top+n^{-2}I_{p+1},
\qquad
\widehat\alpha_{k,h}=\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}\mathbf R_h(X_i)Z_i.
\]
Using the same training indices with \(X_i\ge h\), let \(\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}}\) be the unique minimizer over \(\mathbb R^{J_{\mu,n}}\) of
\[
\frac1{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(X_i)^\top\beta\}^2+n^{-2}\|\beta\|_2^2.
\]
Define the untruncated fit
\[
\widehat\mu^{(-k)}_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)=
\begin{cases}
\mathbf R_h(x)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h},&0\le x<h,\\
\mathbf b_{h,J_{\mu,n}}(x)^\top\widehat\beta_{k,h,J_{\mu,n}},&h\le x\le1.
\end{cases}
\]
Empty local or interior samples return the unique ridge solution. The positive ridges and ordered bases make every fold fit unique. No clipping map or kink derivative is part of the construction.
changed.reason: The former single sieve dimension and clipping derivative do not support the declared nuisance rates or the ordinary boundary linearization. The corrected construction uses the deterministic regression dimension \(J_{\mu,n}\) and an untruncated fit.

changed.from: For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy the nonredundant calibration equations \(\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\). If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J,k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of \[\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).\] Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus \(\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2\). Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the out-of-sample extension \[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(x)=\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J,j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}.\] This formula is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J,1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\): it agrees with that density at every source training atom and is a positive measurable function at independent held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_n=\lceil h_n^{-1}\rceil\).
changed.to:
For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}.
\]
This is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), agrees with that density at source training atoms, and is positive and measurable at held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.
changed.reason: Calibration requires its own deterministic dimension \(J_{r,n}\); tying it to \(h_n^{-1}\) confounds boundary regularization with density-ratio approximation.

changed.from: Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define \[\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J}=\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_h^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.\] Thus each displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), so the residual correction is not an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\).
changed.to:
Using the fold maps \(k_S\) and \(k_T\) and the unique training-complement fits from \(\mathrm{def:regression\text{-}fit}\) and \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\), define
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=
\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_T(j))}(X_j^T)
+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k_S(i))}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k_S(i))}(X_i)\}.
\]
Every displayed evaluation uses a fit trained without that observation's deterministic fold. The dual extension is evaluated as a function at held-out \(X_i\), not as an empirical-support lookup. If an interior training measure is empty, its weight contribution is zero by \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}weights}\). The regression and calibration dimensions are respectively \(J_{\mu,n}\) and \(J_{r,n}\); only \(h\) is the boundary-splice bandwidth.
changed.reason: The estimator must explicitly combine the separately tuned regression and calibration fits while reserving \(h\) for the boundary splice.

changed.from: \[\widehat B_{h,J}=2C_{\mathrm{LP}}Mh^{s+1}+2M\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h,J}(v)|.\] The factor \(2M\) is the Hölder radius inherited by \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\) from the two armwise radius-\(M\) balls, and the displayed support function is indexed by \(J\) through the fitted transport weight inside \(\Delta_{h,J}\).
changed.to:
\[
\widehat B_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=2C_{\mathrm{LP}}Mh^{s+1}+2M\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}|\Delta_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)|.
\]
The factor \(2M\) is the Hölder radius inherited by \(\mu=\mu_1-\mu_0\) from the two armwise radius-\(M\) balls. The regression dimension is displayed because the interval is attached to \(\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\), while the calibration support function itself depends on \(J_{r,n}\) through its fitted transport weight.
changed.reason: The envelope must index the repaired three-argument estimator and the separate calibration residual.

changed.from: For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define the held-out target and interior-residual summands \[\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}=\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_j^T),\qquad \widehat U^R_{i,h,J}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_h^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.\] The source-side linear effect of estimating the boundary polynomial in every fold whose training set contains source observation \(i\) is \[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{k:i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}}{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\left[\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T<h\}\widehat d_{k,h}(X_j^T)\mathbf R_h(X_j^T)^\top\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\right]\{Z_i-\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}.\] Thus \(n^{-1}\sum_i\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}\) is exactly the displayed first-order boundary local-polynomial training contribution to the target plug-in average, with the truncation derivative fixed by \(\widehat d_{k,h}\). For any fold-indexed numbers \((W_u)\), write \(\overline W_k^S=(N_k^S)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}W_i\) and \(\overline W_k^T=(N_k^T)^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}W_j\). Define the fully observable standard error by \[\begin{aligned}\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J}^2={}&\frac1{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^T}{N_k^T-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}(\widehat U^T_{j,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^T}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J})^2\\&+\frac2{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J})(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J}).\end{aligned}\] The four lines are respectively the target variance, interior source variance, boundary source variance, and their within-source covariance. There is no primitive source--target covariance because \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\) is the product experiment; randomness of fold-trained coefficients is retained in every displayed summand and its asymptotic remainder is controlled in the honesty theorem. A term with fold size at most one is defined to be zero.
changed.to:
For \(j\in\mathcal V^T_k\) and \(i\in\mathcal V^S_k\), define
\[
\widehat U^T_{j,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k)}(X_j^T),
\qquad
\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}\{Z_i-\widehat\mu_{h,J_{\mu,n}}^{(-k)}(X_i)\}.
\]
Because the boundary fit is untruncated, its ordinary ridge/local-polynomial linear summand is
\[
\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\frac{n}{m}\sum_{k:i\in\mathcal T^S_k}\frac{\mathbf 1\{X_i\le2h\}}{|\mathcal T^S_k|}\left[\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T<h\}\mathbf R_h(X_j^T)^\top\widehat G_{k,h}^{-1}\mathbf R_h(X_i)\right]\{Z_i-\mathbf R_h(X_i)^\top\widehat\alpha_{k,h}\}.
\]
For fold-indexed numbers \((W_u)\), write \(\overline W_k^S=(N_k^S)^{-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}W_i\) and \(\overline W_k^T=(N_k^T)^{-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}W_j\). Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat{\mathrm{se}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}^2={}&\frac1{m^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^T}{N_k^T-1}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}(\widehat U^T_{j,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^T}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})^2\\
&+\frac2{n^2}\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\frac{N_k^S}{N_k^S-1}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}(\widehat U^R_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^R}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}})(\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\overline{\widehat U^B}_{k,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The four lines are the target variance, interior source variance, boundary source variance, and within-source covariance. There is no primitive source--target covariance because \(\mathbb P_{n,m}=P_S^{\otimes n}\otimes P_T^{\otimes m}\). A term with fold size at most one is zero.
changed.reason: The foldwise summands must use the repaired nuisance dimensions, and removal of clipping requires the ordinary untruncated local-polynomial linear term.

changed.from: Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make \(\{\zeta_i^S:i=1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\{\zeta_j^T:j=1,\ldots,m\}\) mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define the fold-centered calibration process \[\begin{aligned}\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].\end{aligned}\] Define the boundary contribution, using the exact local-polynomial linear summand from \(\mathrm{def:foldwise\text{-}inference\text{-}statistics}\), by \[\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat U^B_{\ell,h,J}\right].\] The computable random envelope is \[\widehat E_{h,J}=\inf\left\{e\ge0:\mathbb P^*\left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}\left|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J}\right|\le e\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_{n,m}\right)\ge1-\gamma/2\right\}.\] Empty-fold averages are zero; with the deterministic modulo allocation they are absent once \(n,m\ge K_0\). The same source multipliers appear in both source pieces, so their covariance is retained, while all target multipliers are independent of all source multipliers.
changed.to:
Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make the source and target multipliers mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\
&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Define
\[

{"id":"def:ricot-weights","name":"Executable interior RiCOT weights","construction":"For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define
\[

\]
This is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), agrees with that density at source training atoms, and is positive and measurable at held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. {"id":"def:calibration-residual-envelope","name":"Multiplier calibration-residual envelope","construction":"Conditionally on \(\mathcal D_{n,m}\), let \(\mathbb P^*\) make the source and target multipliers mutually independent standard-normal variables. For \(v\in\mathcal H^s(1)\), define
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)={}&\frac1m\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{j\in\mathcal V^T_k}\zeta_j^T\left[v(X_j^T)\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^T}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^T_k}v(X_\ell^T)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell^T\ge h\}\right]\\
&-\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_i)v(X_i)\mathbf 1\{X_i\ge h\}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(X_\ell)v(X_\ell)\mathbf 1\{X_\ell\ge h\}\right].
\end{aligned}
\]
Define
\[
\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{K_0}\sum_{i\in\mathcal V^S_k}\zeta_i^S\left[\widehat U^B_{i,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\frac1{N_k^S}\sum_{\ell\in\mathcal V^S_k}\widehat U^B_{\ell,h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right]
\]
and
\[
\widehat E_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\inf\left\{e\ge0:\mathbb P^*\left(\sup_{v\in\mathcal H^s(1)}\left|2M\mathbb G^{\mathrm{cal},*}_{h,J_{r,n}}(v)+\mathbb G^{\mathrm{bd},*}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}\right|\le e\,\middle|\,\mathcal D_{n,m}\right)\ge1-\gamma/2\right\}.

For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. Let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the associated KKT multipliers for nonconstant calibration and the target-marginal equations; among all dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}.
\]
This is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), agrees with that density at source training atoms, and is positive and measurable at held-out points. If either interior training measure is zero, set the extension to zero. The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.

changed.reason: The quadratic-penalty fallback can create exponentially large held-out dual continuations on rare infeasible samples. Capping at the known oracle envelope on the retained interior removes this formula-level tail defect without truncating the true density ratio.

\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.

\[

-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z),
\qquad

\[

\[

\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[

\[

\[
\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}(x)
-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z),
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=2\xi_n\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}},
\]
which is the gradient multiplier contributed by the quadratic calibration penalty, and let \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be a KKT multiplier for the target-marginal equations; among compatible target-marginal multipliers choose the one of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the raw KKT continuation
\[
\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=
\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}
\]
and the capped downstream weight
\[

\]

The cap does not truncate the oracle ratio on \([h,1]\), because \(r(x)=x^{-a}g_T(x)/g_S(x)\le(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}\). The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.
changed.reason: The capped formula distinguishes the downstream weight from the raw KKT continuation, but the zero-interior-mass case currently leaves the primal optimizer and dual variables undefined and can be infeasible when only the source interior measure is zero. The corrected construction handles that measurable branch before optimization, names the raw continuation separately, and states that only the raw training-atom density inherits exact spline calibration.

Fix integers \(n,m\ge2\), a bandwidth \(h\in(0,1)\), and \(\gamma\in(0,1/2)\). For every \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\), the unchanged spliced estimator and the observable coefficients in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}linear\text{-}coefficients}\) satisfy the exact identity
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})Z_i
\]
and the exact error decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau
={}&\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\{Z_i-\mu(X_i)\}\\
&+\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\mu(X_i)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\mu(X_j^T)\right\}\\
&+\left\{\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\mu(X_j^T)-\tau\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathbb P_{n,m}\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau\right|
\le B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_S(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_T(m)\right\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
For any realized covariate design with \(B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\le b\) and \(\sum_i\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})^2\le g^2\), the displayed certificate radius is at most
\[
b+\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)}\,g+\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)/m}.

For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. If either interior training measure has zero total mass, define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=0\), set every calibration and target-marginal multiplier to zero, and set both the raw continuation and the capped downstream weight to zero on \([h,1]\). This branch precedes all optimization below.

Suppose now that both interior training measures have positive total mass. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. In the exact-feasibility branch, let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the KKT multipliers for the nonconstant calibration and target-marginal equations; among all joint dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. In the penalized branch, set
\[
\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}(x)
-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z),
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=2\xi_n\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}},
\]
which is the gradient multiplier contributed by the quadratic calibration penalty, and let \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be a KKT multiplier for the target-marginal equations; among compatible target-marginal multipliers choose the one of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the raw KKT continuation
\[
\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=
\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}
\]
and the capped downstream weight
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\min\left\{\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x),\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}h^{-a}\right\}.
\]
Only \(\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), and only it agrees with that density at source training atoms. The downstream weight \(\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is its pointwise projection onto \([0,(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}]\). It is positive, measurable, and bounded at held-out points, but after projection it need not satisfy the raw plan's exact spline-calibration equations. The cap does not truncate the oracle ratio on \([h,1]\), because \(r(x)=x^{-a}g_T(x)/g_S(x)\le(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}\). The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.

For integers \(n,m\ge2\) and \(h\in(0,1)\), define the observable Hölder design discrepancy
\[
B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})=
\sup_{\substack{v\in\mathcal H^s(2M)\\ \|v\|_\infty\le1}}
\left|\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})v(X_i)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^mv(X_j^T)\right|.
\]
Equivalently, this is the maximum of the two linear optimization problems obtained by multiplying the expression inside the absolute value by \(+1\) and \(-1\), over the convex Hölder feasible set. {"id":"def:ricot-weights","name":"Executable interior RiCOT weights","construction":"For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. If either interior training measure has zero total mass, define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=0\), set every calibration and target-marginal multiplier to zero, and set both the raw continuation and the capped downstream weight to zero on \([h,1]\). This branch precedes all optimization below.

Suppose now that both interior training measures have positive total mass. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. In the exact-feasibility branch, let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the KKT multipliers for the nonconstant calibration and target-marginal equations; among all joint dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. In the penalized branch, set
\[
\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}(x)
-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z),
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=2\xi_n\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}},
\]
which is the gradient multiplier contributed by the quadratic calibration penalty, and let \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be a KKT multiplier for the target-marginal equations; among compatible target-marginal multipliers choose the one of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the raw KKT continuation
\[
\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=
\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}
\]
and the capped downstream weight
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\min\left\{\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x),\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}h^{-a}\right\}.
\]
Only \(\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), and only it agrees with that density at source training atoms. The downstream weight \(\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is its pointwise projection onto \([0,(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}]\). It is positive, measurable, and bounded at held-out points, but after projection it need not satisfy the raw plan's exact spline-calibration equations. The cap does not truncate the oracle ratio on \([h,1]\), because \(r(x)=x^{-a}g_T(x)/g_S(x)\le(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}\). The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.

Both the raw continuation and the capped downstream weight are measurable functions of the observed covariates. In the execution certificate the capped downstream weight enters only through the observable coefficients \(\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\). The cap still does not inherit the raw plan's exact spline-calibration equations, and no held-out localization, coefficient-norm rate, leverage bound, or frontier attainment is claimed.","free_symbols":["\widehat P^S_h","\widehat P^T_h","\widehat\Pi_{h,J}","\mathbf b_{h,J}","\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}","\widehat\theta_{h,J}","\widehat\psi_{h,J}","k","\mathcal T^T_k","c_{\mathrm{OT}}","\eta_0","\lambda_0","\xi_n","n","J_{r,n}","h_n","a","c_{T,+}","c_{S,-}","r","\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT}}_{h,J}","\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT}}_{h,J}"],"inputs":["\mathcal D_{n,m}","h_n","J_{r,n}"]}

\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=

\[
\mathfrak R_{n,m}(a,s,t)\ge c\left\{m^{-1/2}+\begin{cases}
n^{-1/2},&a<1,\\
\sqrt{\log n/n},&a=1,\\
n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)},&a>1.
\end{cases}\right\}.
\]
This lower phase diagram requires no strict slack in the target-density bounds. Moreover, uniformly over \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\),
\[
m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}+n^{-1/2}\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h_n\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}
\asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).
\]
Thus the proved minimax lower frontier matches the exact truncated-oracle envelope; no data-driven minimax upper bound is asserted.

Suppose now that both interior training measures have positive total mass. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)=\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}\,d\Pi_1-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. In the exact-feasibility branch, let \(\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the KKT multipliers for the nonconstant calibration and target-marginal equations; among all joint dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. In the penalized branch, set
\[
\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=
\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}(x)
-\int\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z),
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=2\xi_n\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}},
\]
which is the gradient multiplier contributed by the quadratic calibration penalty, and let \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be a KKT multiplier for the target-marginal equations; among compatible target-marginal multipliers choose the one of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the raw KKT continuation
\[
\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=
\left[\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}
\]
and the capped downstream weight
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\min\left\{\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x),\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}h^{-a}\right\}.

The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration dimension.

{"id":"def:ricot-weights","name":"Executable interior RiCOT weights and certificate role","construction":"For each fold \(k\), form \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\) and \(\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) from the training complements. Put
\[
d_{r,n}=J_{r,n}+q,
\qquad
\mathbf b_{h,J_{r,n}}=(N_1,\ldots,N_{d_{r,n}})^\top,
\]
where \((N_1,\ldots,N_{d_{r,n}})\) is the standard left-to-right normalized degree-\(q\) B-spline basis for the \(J_{r,n}\) endpoint-repeated equally spaced knot intervals on \([h,1]\). Define the equivalent calibration coordinates
\[
\boldsymbol\phi_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\bigl(1,N_2(x),\ldots,N_{d_{r,n}}(x)\bigr)^\top,
\qquad
\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=\bigl(N_2(x),\ldots,N_{d_{r,n}}(x)\bigr)^\top
\in\mathbb R^{d_{r,n}-1}.
\]
The partition-of-unity identity gives
\[
N_1(x)=1-\sum_{\ell=2}^{d_{r,n}}N_\ell(x),
\]
so \(\boldsymbol\phi_{h,J_{r,n}}\) and \(\mathbf b_{h,J_{r,n}}\) span the same spline space.

If either interior training measure has zero total mass, define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=0\), set the calibration vector in \(\mathbb R^{d_{r,n}-1}\) and every target-marginal multiplier to zero, and set both the raw continuation and the capped downstream weight to zero on \([h,1]\). This branch precedes all optimization below.

Suppose now that both interior training measures have positive total mass. Let \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\) be the finite plans \(\Pi\) that have strictly positive density relative to \(\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), satisfy \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), and satisfy
\[
\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)
=\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z).
\]
Because \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\) implies
\[
\Pi_1([h,1])=\Pi_2([h,1])=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h([h,1]),
\]
the separate target-mass constraint supplies the constant coordinate. Together with the preceding \(d_{r,n}-1\) equations and the identity for \(N_1\), it is equivalent to calibration of the full space \(\mathcal B_{h,J_{r,n}}\).

If \(\mathcal F^\circ_{h,J_{r,n},k}\ne\varnothing\), define \(\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) as the unique minimizer over its closure of
\[
\int c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,z)\,d\Pi
+\eta_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\otimes\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h)
+\lambda_0\operatorname{KL}(\Pi_1\,\|\,\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h).
\]
Otherwise minimize the same strictly convex criterion subject to \(\Pi_2=\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h\), plus
\[
\xi_n\left\|
\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\Pi_1(x)
-\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z)
\right\|_2^2.
\]
Generalized Kullback--Leibler divergence is used for finite measures. In the exact-feasibility branch, let
\[
\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\in\mathbb R^{d_{r,n}-1}
\]
and \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be the KKT multipliers for the nonconstant calibration and target-marginal equations; among all joint dual solutions choose the pair of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. In the penalized branch, set
\[
\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=
\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)\,d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}(x)
-\int\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(z)\,d\widehat P^{T,(-k)}_h(z),
\qquad
\widehat\theta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}=2\xi_n\widehat\delta^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}
\in\mathbb R^{d_{r,n}-1},
\]
and let \(\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}\) be a KKT multiplier for the target-marginal equations; among compatible target-marginal multipliers choose the one of smallest Euclidean norm, with lexicographic tie-breaking. For every \(x\in[h,1]\), define the raw KKT continuation
\[
\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)=
\left[
\frac1{|\mathcal T^T_k|}\sum_{j\in\mathcal T^T_k}\mathbf 1\{X_j^T\ge h\}
\exp\left\{-\frac{c_{\mathrm{OT}}(x,X_j^T)
+\widehat\theta_{h,J_{r,n}}^{(-k)\top}\widetilde{\boldsymbol\phi}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)
+\widehat\psi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},j}}{\eta_0}\right\}
\right]^{\eta_0/(\eta_0+\lambda_0)}
\]
and the capped downstream weight
\[
\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x)
=\min\left\{\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}(x),\frac{c_{T,+}}{c_{S,-}}h^{-a}\right\}.
\]
Only \(\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is the KKT continuation of \(d\widehat\Pi^{(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n},1}/d\widehat P^{S,(-k)}_h\), and only it agrees with that density at source training atoms. The downstream weight \(\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT},(-k)}_{h,J_{r,n}}\) is its pointwise projection onto \([0,(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}]\). It is positive, measurable, and bounded at held-out points, but after projection it need not satisfy the raw plan's exact spline-calibration equations. The cap does not truncate the oracle ratio on \([h,1]\), because \(r(x)=x^{-a}g_T(x)/g_S(x)\le(c_{T,+}/c_{S,-})h^{-a}\). The deterministic schedules are \(\eta_n=\eta_0\), \(\lambda_n=\lambda_0\), \(\xi_n=n^2\), and \(J=J_{r,n}\); the boundary-splice bandwidth remains \(h=h_n\) and is not used as the calibration knot-interval count.

Both the raw continuation and the capped downstream weight are measurable functions of the observed covariates. In the execution certificate the capped downstream weight enters only through the observable coefficients \(\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\). The cap still does not inherit the raw plan's exact spline-calibration equations, and no held-out localization, coefficient-norm rate, leverage bound, or frontier attainment is claimed.","free_symbols":["\widehat P^S_h","\widehat P^T_h","\widehat\Pi_{h,J}","\mathbf b_{h,J}","\widetilde{\mathbf b}_{h,J}","\widehat\theta_{h,J}","\widehat\psi_{h,J}","k","\mathcal T^T_k","c_{\mathrm{OT}}","\eta_0","\lambda_0","\xi_n","n","J_{r,n}","h_n","a","c_{T,+}","c_{S,-}","r","\widetilde r^{\mathrm{KKT}}_{h,J}","\widehat r^{\mathrm{RICOT}}_{h,J}","\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})"],"inputs":["\mathcal D_{n,m}","h_n","J_{r,n}"]}

{"id":"thm:adaptive-handle-not-executable","kind":"theorem","statement":"The multiscale handle in \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\) does not, as presently constructed, define a single interval-valued statistic. It specifies neither measurable exponent estimators, thresholds, a selection rule, nor tie breaking. Consequently the frozen construction has no coverage probability or expected length to evaluate and does not yield the proposed adaptive guarantee. A positive result requires a new executable construction before self-similarity can be used to prove adaptation.","free_symbols":["\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}","a","J_{\mu,n}","J_{r,n}"],"depends_on":["def:adaptive-handle"],"status":"to-prove","justification":"This negative answer isolates the formal obstruction before any adaptive coverage claim is attempted.","gap":"The frozen multiscale handle is descriptive rather than an executable selection rule, so existing self-similarity theory cannot yet be applied to it.","consumer":"A downstream construction must specify the measurable diagnostics, thresholds, selection map, and tie breaking before it can be used in the RICOT cardiomyopathy analysis.","proof_tex":"\textbf{Proof.}
Let
\[
\mathsf D_{n,m}
=\bigl(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}\times[0,1]\bigr)^n\times\mathcal X^m
\]
carry its product Borel \(\sigma\)-field. An interval-valued statistic must, at a minimum, be a single-valued measurable map
\[
T_{n,m}:\mathsf D_{n,m}\longrightarrow
\bigl\{[\ell,u]:\ell,u\in\mathbb R,\ \ell\le u\bigr\}.
\]
Equivalently, it must specify measurable endpoint functions \(L_{n,m}\) and \(U_{n,m}\) satisfying
\[
T_{n,m}(d)=[L_{n,m}(d),U_{n,m}(d)]
\quad\text{and}\quad
L_{n,m}(d)\le U_{n,m}(d)
\]
for every realized data array \(d\in\mathsf D_{n,m}\).

By \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\), the candidate family is
\[
\left\{\mathcal I_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}:
h\text{ is an admissible dyadic boundary bandwidth}\right\}.
\]
The construction instructs the user to form adjacent-scale boundary local-polynomial differences, to estimate \(a\) from empirical masses of dyadic boundary shells, and to combine these quantities with interior Riesz-calibration residuals. It gives no formula for a measurable estimator of \(a\) or of the boundary regularity, no numerical threshold for an adjacent-scale comparison, no rule mapping the resulting diagnostics to one admissible dyadic \(h\), and no convention for choosing among multiple admissible candidates.

Consequently, the construction specifies neither endpoint functions \(L_{n,m},U_{n,m}\) nor an equivalent measurable bandwidth selector
\[
\widehat h_{n,m}:\mathsf D_{n,m}\longrightarrow
\{h:h\text{ is an admissible dyadic boundary bandwidth}\}
\]
such that
\[
T_{n,m}(d)
=\mathcal I_{\widehat h_{n,m}(d),J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}(d).
\]
Equivalently, it does not specify a measurable selected triple
\[
\bigl(\widehat h_{n,m},J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}\bigr).
\]

This is a definitional obstruction, not a stochastic remainder. The self-similarity restriction invoked by the handle restricts the member law; it does not itself select a bandwidth for a realized data array. The written handle is compatible with distinct completions that choose different dyadic bandwidths whenever several candidates satisfy an unspecified comparison, and the handle selects none of those completions. Hence it does not define a single interval-valued statistic.

Because the handle defines no random interval \(T_{n,m}\), neither
\[
\mathbb P_{n,m}\!\left\{\tau\in T_{n,m}(\mathcal D_{n,m})\right\}
\]
nor
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbb P_{n,m}}\!\left[
U_{n,m}(\mathcal D_{n,m})-L_{n,m}(\mathcal D_{n,m})
\right]
\]
is an evaluable quantity attached to \(\mathrm{def:adaptive\text{-}handle}\). The frozen handle therefore yields neither an adaptive coverage guarantee nor an adaptive expected-length guarantee. A positive result first requires explicit measurable diagnostics, numerical thresholds, a single-valued dyadic-bandwidth selection rule, and deterministic tie breaking. This proves the theorem. \(\square\)"}

For integers \(n,m\ge2\) and \(h\in(0,1)\), define the observable Hölder design discrepancy
\[
B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})=
\sup_{\substack{v\in\mathcal H^s(2M)\\ \|v\|_\infty\le1}}
\left|\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})v(X_i)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^mv(X_j^T)\right|.
\]
Equivalently, this is the maximum of the two linear optimization problems obtained by multiplying the expression inside the absolute value by \(+1\) and \(-1\), over the convex Hölder feasible set. Thus it is an exact covariate-measurable verification object. No polynomial-time evaluation claim and no stochastic-order or frontier-order claim is part of the definition.
changed.to:
For this certificate use the following H\"older convention. Put \(p=\lceil s\rceil-1\) and \(\beta=s-p\in(0,1]\). For \(L>0\),
\[
\mathcal H^s(L)=\left\{v\in C^p([0,1]):
\max_{0\le r\le p}\|v^{(r)}\|_\infty\le L,
\quad
[v^{(p)}]_{\beta}:=\sup_{x\ne y}\frac{|v^{(p)}(x)-v^{(p)}(y)|}{|x-y|^\beta}\le L
\right\}.
\]
For integers \(n,m\ge2\) and \(h\in(0,1)\), let \(z_1<\cdots<z_N\) be the distinct sites among \(X_1,\ldots,X_n,X_1^T,\ldots,X_m^T\), and set
\[
c_\ell=\sum_{i:X_i=z_\ell}\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})-
\frac1m\#\{j:X_j^T=z_\ell\}.
\]
Retain the abstract design discrepancy
\[
B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})=
\sup_{\substack{v\in\mathcal H^s(2M)\\ \|v\|_\infty\le1}}
\left|\sum_{\ell=1}^Nc_\ell v(z_\ell)\right|.
\]
For each \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\), let \(V_\sigma\) be the optimal value of the finite linear program
\[
\operatorname{maximize}_{(u_{\ell,r})}\quad
\sigma\sum_{\ell=1}^Nc_\ell u_{\ell,0}
\]
over \(N(p+1)\) real variables \(u_{\ell,r}\), \(1\le\ell\le N\), \(0\le r\le p\), subject to
\[
|u_{\ell,0}|\le1,
\qquad
|u_{\ell,r}|\le2M\quad(1\le r\le p),
\]
and, for every \(1\le\ell,k\le N\) and \(0\le r\le p\),
\[
\left|u_{\ell,r}-\sum_{q=r}^p
u_{k,q}\frac{(z_\ell-z_k)^{q-r}}{(q-r)!}\right|
\le
2M\frac{\Gamma(\beta+1)}{\Gamma(s-r+1)}|z_\ell-z_k|^{s-r}.
\]
Each absolute-value restriction means its two one-sided linear inequalities. Define the certified jet-LP radius
\[
\overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})=\max\{V_{-1},V_1\}.
\]
The two programs have \(N(p+1)\) variables and \(O\{N^2(p+1)\}\) linear inequalities. Every admissible H\"older trace is feasible, so
\[
B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\le\overline B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}).
\]
For \(0<s\le1\) the reduction is exact by H\"older--McShane extension. For \(s>1\) it is a certified conservative jet relaxation, not an asserted exact finite Whitney characterization. Both optimal values are finite because of the box constraints. No stochastic-order or frontier-order claim is part of this definition.

Fix integers \(n,m\ge2\), a bandwidth \(h\in(0,1)\), and \(\gamma\in(0,1/2)\). For every \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\), the unchanged spliced estimator and the observable coefficients in \(\mathrm{def:ricot\text{-}linear\text{-}coefficients}\) satisfy the exact identity
\[
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}=\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})Z_i
\]
and the exact error decomposition
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau
={}&\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\{Z_i-\mu(X_i)\}\\
&+\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\mu(X_i)-\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\mu(X_j^T)\right\}\\
&+\left\{\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m\mu(X_j^T)-\tau\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathbb P_{n,m}\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau^{\mathrm{sp}}_{h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n}}-\tau\right|
\le B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_S(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})+R_T(m)\right\}\ge1-\gamma.
\]
For any realized covariate design with \(B_X(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})\le b\) and \(\sum_i\Gamma_i(h,J_{\mu,n},J_{r,n})^2\le g^2\), the displayed certificate radius is at most
\[
b+\varepsilon^{-1}\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)}\,g+\sqrt{2\log(4/\gamma)/m}.
\]
This is a finite-sample execution certificate. It makes no stochastic-order, localization, leverage, minimax-attainment, or expected-length claim for \(B_X\) or the coefficient norm.

changed.from: For the deterministic regime bandwidth \(h_n\), the truncated oracle representer obeys \[m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}+n^{-1/2}\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h_n\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}\asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).\] Thus the exact boundary-bias and oracle source-standard-deviation balance has the regular, critical, and nonregular rates in \(\mathrm{def:frontier\text{-}rate}\).
changed.to:
For fixed \(a,s,t,M\) with \(M\ge a+1\) and \(t>0\), let \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\), write \(P=(P_S,P_T)\) for its pair of one-observation laws, and let \(h\in(0,1)\). The matrix \(G_h^{\circ}(P)\) is positive definite, and for every polynomial \(\ell\) of degree at most \(p\),
\[
\int_0^h w_h^{\mathrm{BLP}}(x;P)\ell(x)f_S(x)\,dx
=\int_0^h\ell(x)f_T(x)\,dx.
\]
Uniformly over the model class,
\[
\{q_h^{\circ}(P)\}^{\top}\{G_h^{\circ}(P)\}^{-1}q_h^{\circ}(P)\asymp h^{1-a},
\qquad
|\mathfrak b_h(\mu;P)|\le b_h^{\circ}(P)\le C h^{s+1},
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\omega_h^{\circ}(\cdot;P)\|_{L^2(P_S)}^2
&=\{q_h^{\circ}(P)\}^{\top}\{G_h^{\circ}(P)\}^{-1}q_h^{\circ}(P)
+\int_h^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx\\
&\asymp
\begin{cases}
1,&a<1,\\
\log(1/h),&a=1,\\
h^{1-a},&a>1.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\]
For every fixed \(a>0\), the allowance is class-sharp in the sense that, for an admissible member law and all sufficiently small \(h\), \(b_h^{\circ}(P)\ge c h^{s+1}\). At \(a=0\), if \(f_S=f_T\) on \([0,h]\), both \(\mathfrak b_h(\mu;P)\) and \(b_h^{\circ}(P)\) may vanish. Consequently, for the deterministic regime bandwidth \(h_n\),
\[
m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}+n^{-1/2}\|\omega_{h_n}^{\circ}(\cdot;P)\|_{L^2(P_S)}
\asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).
\]
This is a population boundary-local-polynomial linear-weight benchmark. It is not a data-measurable estimator and does not establish a minimax upper bound.
changed.reason: The raw truncated representer omits the boundary contribution and therefore does not itself have the asserted order-\(h^{s+1}\) bias. The boundary local-polynomial construction gives the valid oracle allowance and full linear-weight norm, while permitting zero actual bias for special laws.

\[

n^{-1/2},&a<1,\\
\sqrt{\log n/n},&a=1,\\
n^{-(s+1)/(2s+a+1)},&a>1.
\end{cases}\right\}.
\]
This lower phase diagram requires no strict slack in the target-density bounds. Moreover, uniformly over \(\mathbb P_{n,m}\in\mathcal M_{n,m}(a,s,t)\),
\[
m^{-1/2}+h_n^{s+1}+n^{-1/2}\left\|r\mathbf 1\{X\ge h_n\}\right\|_{L^2(P_S)}
\asymp m^{-1/2}+\rho_n(a,s).
\]
Thus the proved minimax lower frontier matches the exact truncated-oracle envelope; no data-driven minimax upper bound is asserted.

\[
\int_0^h w_h^{\mathrm{BLP}}(x;P)\ell(x)f_S(x)\,dx
=\int_0^h\ell(x)f_T(x)\,dx.

\[
\{q_h^{\circ}(P)\}^{\top}\{G_h^{\circ}(P)\}^{-1}q_h^{\circ}(P)\asymp h^{1-a},
\qquad
|\mathfrak b_h(\mu;P)|\le b_h^{\circ}(P)\le C h^{s+1},
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|\omega_h^{\circ}(\cdot;P)\|_{L^2(P_S)}^2
&=\{q_h^{\circ}(P)\}^{\top}\{G_h^{\circ}(P)\}^{-1}q_h^{\circ}(P)
+\int_h^1\frac{f_T(x)^2}{f_S(x)}\,dx\\
&\asymp
\begin{cases}
1,&a<1,\\
\log(1/h),&a=1,\\
h^{1-a},&a>1.
\end{cases}
\end{aligned}
\]
